content.thinking:
Excellent! The deep peeling chain achieves round depth 996 with 3981 links and takes only 0.08 s. This validates that the incremental peeler is efficient (the naive approach would take 996 rounds × ~8000 path-ASNs = 8M operations, which would be ~5-10 s; the incremental one is much faster).

Let me verify the deep peeling results against the reference (simple) peeler for the k=200 case to make sure the incremental peeler is CORRECT on deep structures.

Let me also compare timing of the naive approach to confirm the value of the incremental one... well, correctness matters more. Let me run the reference peel comparison on the deep chain.

arguments.command:
cd /workspace && python3 - << 'EOF'
import sys, time
sys.path.insert(0, 'tmp'); sys.path.insert(0, 'submission')
import ref, main as M
sys.path.insert(0, 'tmp')
from perf4 import build
for k in (50, 200):
    doc = build(k)
    agg = {}
    for rec in doc['rib']:
        p = tuple(rec['path'])
        agg[p] = agg.get(p,0)+rec['count']
    t0=time.time(); f1, r1 = M.peel(list(agg.items())); t1=time.time()
    t2=time.time(); f2, r2 = ref.ref_peel(dict(agg)); t3=time.time()
    print('k=%d mine %.3fs ref %.3fs agree=%s maxround=%d' % (k, t1-t0, t3-t2, (f1==f2 and r1==r2), max(r1.values())))
EOF
